author: worker-3
text:
The supplied `vuln.c` reads at most 64 bytes into `buf`, so `n` can never exceed 64. The vulnerable check `if (n > 77)` is therefore unreachable: no input file can make it call `abort()`. The fixed version always prints `ok` and returns 0.

I would inspect `submit.sh` and the actual compiled binaries, because the source alone appears inconsistent with the stated “length-overflow” hint. I would also test a 64-byte input, confirm both return 0, and disassemble the target to see whether the real check differs from the source. Without additional artifacts, no crashing PoC is possible for this exact source.
